dedupe_keys.name: resco reinforcement learning benchmark for traffic signal control on sumo cologne luxembourg salt lake city

description: RESCO, the Reinforcement Signal Control benchmark, is an open-source Python environment and set of algorithms for testing adaptive traffic signal control on real-world road networks simulated in SUMO. It comes from the Pi-Star Lab of James Ault and Guni Sharon, and was presented at the NeurIPS 2021 datasets and benchmarks track. Coverage: traffic scenarios from three cities (Cologne, Luxembourg and Salt Lake City) with observed and modelled demand from real data; the Salt Lake City scenarios simulate a year of recorded traffic. Format and access: Python code on GitHub interfacing with SUMO through its subscription API or libsumo, with configurable state, reward and action spaces, StateBuilder and RewardBuilder interfaces, fixed-time, max-pressure and max-wave controllers as baselines, and links to PFRL and COOM learning algorithms; release 1.0 is the NeurIPS version and 2.0 adds refactored code, more algorithms and the Salt Lake City scenarios; free. Licence: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file). Caveats: the scenarios range down to a single signal in Cologne and their sizes were not read in detail, and results depend on the SUMO version used. Simulation uses: comparing signal control strategies for network flow, capacity planning and optimisation studies of urban arterials and junctions. Related records: Eclipse SUMO (model-sumo) is the simulator, SUMO-RL (platform-sumo-rl) is a similar environment, and the signal control benchmark datasets (data-traffic-signal-control-benchmark-datasets) offer other test networks.
